rĕ-mando , ĕre, v. a.,
I.to chew over again, to chew the cud, ruminate (postAug.): “Pontici mures simili modo remandunt,” Plin. 10, 73, 93, § 200 : “taedium scripta et lecta saepius revolvendi et quasi eundem cibum remandendi,” Quint. 11, 2, 41 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
